title: Martial Arts Instructor (MGySgt to Cpl) FMOS, CG TECOM
raw_text:
5.     MOS 0916, Martial Arts Instructor (MGySgt to Cpl) FMOS, CG TECOM

    a. Summary. Martial Arts Instructors conduct training in principles of
close combat and core values.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must qualify first class on CFT.

            (2) Must qualify first class on the PFT.

            (3) Must be certified as gray belt or above.

            (4) Must have recommendation of reporting senior.

        (5) Must be a corporal or above.         This prerequisite is non-
waiverable.



                                          3-93                          Enclosure (1)
 3115                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



        (6) Full duty status shoulder injury free in previous 2 years,
concussion free within the past 6 months and free of contagious diseases or
dermatological conditions.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Must complete the appropriate level PME for grade.

        (2) Successful completion of the CG TRNGCOM approved Martial Arts
Instructor Course (M02MMET).

    d. Duties.       Trains and certifies personnel from tan through 1st degree
black belt.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   Martial Arts Instructor-Trainer, 0917.
common_text: Occupational Field 09, Training, comprises MOSs used to identify Marines who possess skill sets to conduct vital training, particularly to entry-level Marines, as required by various high visibility Marine Corps programs. First exposure to Marine Corps training is provided by the Drill Instructor. Next contact is with the marksmanship coaches and instructors overseen by a Range Officer, Swim Instructors, Martial Arts Instructors, and then Marine Combat Instructors. In the operating forces, training continues with the addition of Small Weapons Instructors and Martial Arts Instructor-Trainers. These MOSs are sponsored by the Training and Education Command.

Occupational Field 09, Training, comprises MOSs used to identify Marines who possess skill sets to conduct vital training, particularly to entry-level Marines, as required by various high visibility Marine Corps programs. First exposure to Marine Corps training is provided by the Drill Instructor. Next contact is with the marksmanship coaches and instructors overseen by a Range Officer, Swim Instructors, Martial Arts Instructors, and then Marine Combat Instructors. In the operating forces, training continues with the addition of Small Weapons Instructors and Martial Arts Instructor-Trainers. These MOSs are sponsored by the Training and Education Command.

5. MOS 0916, Martial Arts Instructor (MGySgt to Cpl) FMOS, CG TECOM a. Summary. Martial Arts Instructors conduct training in principles of close combat and core values. b. Prerequisites (1) Must qualify first class on CFT. (2) Must qualify first class on the PFT. (3) Must be certified as gray belt or above. (4) Must have recommendation of reporting senior. (5) Must be a corporal or above. This prerequisite is non- waiverable. (6) Full duty status shoulder injury free in previous 2 years, concussion free within the past 6 months and free of contagious diseases or dermatological conditions. c. Requirements (1) Must complete the appropriate level PME for grade. (2) Successful completion of the CG TRNGCOM approved Martial Arts Instructor Course (M02MMET). d. Duties. Trains and certifies personnel from tan through 1st degree black belt.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
